# spry-turn

> Lightweight Rust STUN/TURN server, embeddable native relay and WASM packet codec. MIT; maintained by TheCryptoDonkey under ForgeSworn.

Version 0.3.0. Source and GitHub prereleases are public, under MIT, copyright 2026 TheCryptoDonkey. There is no crates.io, docs.rs or npm publication, hosted relay, credential service or public documentation site.

Native UDP/TCP clients and optional TLS use UDP peer allocations. Browser applications use their existing WebRTC ICE implementation. Ordinary browser WASM cannot host a raw-socket TURN server. Shared TURN secrets belong only to trusted operator tools; give clients short-lived credentials.

This is an initial implementation, without full coturn parity or production qualification. UDP peer-relay port ranges are optional and fail closed on exhaustion. Static user databases, TCP relay allocations, DTLS and dual allocations are not implemented. Archipelago private packaging has separate qualification; native desktop/Android hosting controls and general physical-phone/public-network acceptance remain open. Sapflow integration remains a later goal.

The full v0.2.1 native ARM64 M4 Max loopback matrix measured 16–22% higher UDP delivery rate and 27–35% higher TLS delivery rate than the tested coturn configuration; TCP ranged from 1.2% behind to 8.5% ahead. Linux VM results differ, including UDP regressions. These are workload results, not maximum WAN capacity. Stream and kernel socket memory have separate costs. Consult current qualification and raw evidence before reusing figures.

These files provide navigation and source context for readers and tools. They do not change repository visibility or guarantee indexing by search engines or language models.

Generated by scripts/docs.mjs; edit source guides and run npm run docs:generate.

## Source: Overview

Canonical source: [README.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/README.md)

# spry-turn

A lightweight standalone **STUN/TURN server in Rust**, an embeddable native
library and a portable **WebAssembly packet codec**. UDP and TCP clients,
optional TLS, coturn-compatible shared-secret credentials, bounded resources
and no media stack. MIT licensed, copyright 2026 TheCryptoDonkey. The source and GitHub prereleases are public.

[Documentation](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/README.md) · [Quick start](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md) ·
[WebRTC and native integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md) ·
[Coturn compatibility](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/coturn-compatibility.md) ·
[API](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md) · [Support development](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/SUPPORT.md#donations) ·
[LLM index](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/llms.txt)

The full v0.2.1 native M4 Max loopback matrix measured **16–22% more UDP
packets/s** and **27–35% more TLS packets/s** than the tested coturn
configuration. TCP ranged from 1.2% behind to 8.5% ahead. These are delivered
rates for six workload cells per transport, with bounded relay ports and
TLS enabled in the Rust build. Linux VM results differ, including UDP
regressions. Process RSS excludes kernel socket memory.
See [current measurements and limitations](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/qualification-0.2.1.md)
and the [historical UDP comparison](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).

The first target is a server running independently on a normal computer.
Later, an Archy owner can install it and configure KithMoot to use their
chosen TURN address and credentials. The software publisher operates no
relay, credential service, discovery directory or calling entitlement.
There are no hosted defaults in the code. An independent operator can opt
in to [public mode](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/public-mode.md), opening their own relay to anyone
and optionally advertising it on Nostr relays they choose; it is off by
default.

Spry is independent of Archipelago. The reusable `spry-turn`, `spry-access`,
`spry-link` and `spry-service` Rust libraries live here, together with a standalone
pairing service. Archipelago is an optional package and host integration.
See [standalone use and library boundaries](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/standalone.md).

## What works

- STUN Binding, authenticated TURN Allocate and Refresh, CreatePermission,
  ChannelBind, Send/Data indications and ChannelData.
- UDP relaying, with clients connecting over UDP or TCP. The `tls` feature
  adds TLS 1.2/1.3 client connections using rustls.
- Optional inclusive UDP peer-relay port range, with occupied-port skipping,
  authenticated 508 on exhaustion and no allocation outside the range.
- Coturn-compatible TURN REST credentials: expiry-prefixed usernames and
  a shared secret. Credential generation is an operator-run local command.
- IPv4 or IPv6 relay address family per configured instance. Native IPv6
  sockets and XOR address encoding are supported; dual allocations are not.
- Expiring allocations, IP permissions and channel bindings; bounded
  allocations, per-user allocations, connections, peers, stream buffers,
  control request rate and per-allocation bandwidth.
- Private, loopback, link-local and multicast targets blocked by default.
  Explicit loopback testing is restricted to a loopback-only listener.
- The forwarding library has no media decoders, WebRTC stack, database,
  async runtime, admin website, analytics, access log or room membership.
  The separate access and service crates provide optional owner-run pairing.

The UDP ChannelData path borrows incoming payloads and reserves header space
in its receive buffer, avoiding a payload copy on the return path. One
non-blocking Mio event loop owns sockets and allocation state; no per-packet
tasks or worker queues. Generation-tagged slots route readiness events
without hashing internal tokens and reject stale events after reuse.
TCP/TLS uses bounded output buffers and updates writable readiness only
when backpressure changes, avoiding a registration syscall per packet.
The library forbids unsafe Rust in its own code; dependencies may use it.

Concrete IPv4 listeners use a connected client-facing UDP socket per
allocation to retain the client's fixed five-tuple in the kernel. This
improves the measured send/receive path and costs one additional UDP socket
per client. Wildcard/IPv6 listeners and unavailable fast-path sockets retain
standard forwarding. The portable build is available with
`--no-default-features --features runtime,turn`. RSS measurements exclude
kernel socket memory; see the comparison's socket counts and limitations.

This is an initial implementation, not full coturn parity or a production
qualification. [Compatibility and remaining work](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md) are explicit.

## Run locally

Rust 1.85 or later; stable Rust 1.94 is tested. Build output uses `target/`.

```sh
cargo build --release
export SPRY_TURN_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
./target/release/spry-turn serve
```

The default UDP/TCP listener is `127.0.0.1:3478`. Generate a short-lived
credential locally using the same environment:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn credential --ttl 3600 --label client
```

For larger workloads, size the process file-descriptor limit for listeners,
two sockets per optimised UDP allocation and any TCP/TLS connections.
`--max-allocations` limits logical allocations; it cannot raise an OS limit.
The comparison runner raises its own descriptor floor towards 4,096 where
the hard limit permits, and records the actual inherited limit.

Use an opaque transport label. Do not put room IDs, personal identities or
application membership in usernames. The credential output is a secret;
do not commit it or put it in public logs. The shared secret never belongs
in a browser, join URL or client build. Operators decide how to give their
own users credentials; no remotely callable credential issuer is included.

Configure a standard ICE client with `turn:HOST:3478?transport=udp` or
`turn:HOST:3478?transport=tcp`, the generated username and credential. A
website uses its browser's existing WebRTC support; it does not host TURN.

To listen on a chosen interface, supply `--listen IP:PORT` and, if needed,
`--relay-ip IP`. Wildcard listeners require an explicit concrete relay IP.
`--public-ip IP` advertises an operator-configured NAT address. The
operator must provide actual reachability and firewall rules; installing
the server cannot make an inaccessible home connection a public relay.

Use `--relay-ports 49160:49191` to bound peer UDP allocations for an
operator-controlled firewall/NAT configuration. Without it, allocations
retain OS-assigned ephemeral ports. See [the operator guide](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md)
for reachability, resource budgets and port-preserving NAT requirements.

TLS is optional at build time:

```sh
cargo build --release --features tls
./target/release/spry-turn serve --tls-listen 127.0.0.1:5349 \
  --tls-cert certificate.pem --tls-key private-key.pem
```

Use a certificate trusted by the intended clients. Local tests generate
temporary certificates and test trust separately from public deployment.
The process has no certificate renewal or TLS file watcher yet.

## Embed

`spry_turn::turn::Server::bind(Config)` creates a server;
`poll_once(Duration)` advances its event loop. The host controls its lifetime
and configuration. No threads are started by the library. Build with
`--no-default-features --features turn` for the borrowed wire codec and
credential helpers without the socket runtime. Swift/Kotlin bindings and
physical phone acceptance are later work.

## WebAssembly

The portable packet codec and credential helpers also build to WASM,
without Mio, socket2, TLS or an OS random-number dependency:

```sh
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  --no-default-features --features wasm --lib
wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir .local/wasm --out-name spry_turn \
  target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/spry_turn.wasm
node tests/wasm.mjs
```

Use wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129 to match the pinned bindings. `PacketArena`
provides a reusable region of linear memory that a host accesses through
`Uint8Array`. Channel framing/parsing reuses that region without per-packet
Rust allocations or whole-payload binding marshalling. Recreate the view
after memory growth and do not retain it after freeing the arena.

The initial module is about 56 kB. A real WASM execution test validates the
published STUN integrity vector and repeats a million framing/parsing
operations without growing linear memory. That is a protocol microbenchmark,
separate from server network throughput. Networking and allocation/session
I/O belong to the native server adapter; ordinary browser WASM cannot host
a standard raw-socket TURN server.

TURN forwards arbitrary datagrams; it has no WebRTC media semantics. A
future SRT/Sapflow client could use an appropriate transport adapter.
Unmodified SRT/RTMP applications do not automatically speak TURN. Sapflow
integration and transparent UDP forwarding are not implemented here.

## Verify

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-features
cargo test --no-default-features --lib
cargo test --no-default-features --features turn --lib
cargo build --release --features tls
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium
python3 tests/browser.py --tls
```

The independent Python stdlib client checks real UDP/TCP/TLS sockets.
Chromium forces relay/relay candidates and verifies generated video decoded,
audio received and application data returned in both directions for all
three client transports. Browser tests use a generated test certificate and
explicit browser certificate bypass; the Python TLS test validates its
generated CA. This is not public-certificate or real-phone acceptance.

The [comparison runner](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/scripts/compare.py) uses the same socket-level load
generator against each server, alternating order. It reports delivered
packets, loss/corruption, round-trip latency, RSS and server CPU. All test
servers bind loopback and clean up their processes and generated secrets.

## Scope and legal position

The chosen role is publishing software, with independent owners operating
their own relay instances. The [transport position](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/legal/transport-position.md)
records that architecture and the unresolved legal interpretations. A
private repository, MIT licence, encryption or use of TURN does not by
itself determine a future operator's Online Safety Act position.

MIT applies to our code. Dependency notices are in
[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt); published RFC test data
is credited in [NOTICE](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/NOTICE). There is no package publication or hosted
service deployment in this repository.

# spry-turn documentation

spry-turn is a standalone Rust STUN/TURN server, an embeddable native relay
and a WASM packet codec. It is an initial implementation with measured
performance and explicit compatibility gaps. The source and GitHub prereleases are public and MIT-licensed; there is no publisher-operated TURN service.

## Source: Getting started

Canonical source: [docs/getting-started.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)

# Getting started

This guide runs a local standalone server. It does not expose a public
relay or require a hosted service. See [operations](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md) before
configuring an independently operated instance.

## Obtain the source

The source is public and MIT-licensed. Clone it without a GitHub account:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn.git
cd spry-turn
```

Source is the portable installation path. Cargo and npm publication are
disabled. The public v0.3.0 GitHub prerelease carries the TLS-enabled macOS
ARM64 `spry-turn` executable with checksums and a build manifest. Fetch and
verify it in an empty directory:

```sh
gh release download v0.3.0 --repo forgesworn/spry-turn
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

[Download v0.3.0](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/releases/tag/v0.3.0).
Linux, Windows, WASM and `spry-node` are source builds for this version.
The [older v0.2.1 release](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/releases/tag/v0.2.1)
retains its original macOS/Linux ARM64 and WASM archives; those do not contain
the newer options. Existing archives and tags retain their original bytes.
A release does not establish production or physical-device acceptance.

Rust 1.85 or newer is declared; Rust 1.94.1 and 1.96 were used for the
initial verification and native M4 measurements. Current CI checks stable
Rust on Linux and macOS. Python 3, Node 24, OpenSSL and Chromium are test
tools, not server runtime dependencies.

## Build and start

```sh
cargo build --locked --release
export SPRY_TURN_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
./target/release/spry-turn serve
```

The process binds UDP and TCP at `127.0.0.1:3478`. Keep this terminal running;
stop it with Ctrl-C. The secret must contain at least 32 bytes. This example
generates a fresh one; a real operator must store and supply their chosen
secret consistently across restarts and credential generation.

The server blocks loopback peers by default, even when its listener is
local. The following explicit local-test mode allows two local ICE clients
to send traffic through it:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn serve --allow-loopback-peers
```

Stop the first server before starting the second command on the same port.
Loopback-peer testing is restricted to a loopback-only listener and is
unnecessary for normal public-address peers.

## Generate client credentials

Use the same secret in a separate shell or generate the credential before
starting the server:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn credential --ttl 3600 --label client
```

The command emits JSON with `username` and `credential`. TTL is 1–86,400
seconds. Labels are 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.
Use an opaque transport label rather than a room name or identity.

Give the client that short-lived pair through an operator-controlled
channel. The client must never receive `SPRY_TURN_SECRET`. Credential output
is sensitive; do not paste it into an issue, log or committed fixture.
See [integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md) for ICE configuration.

## Optional TLS

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --features tls
./target/release/spry-turn serve --tls-listen 127.0.0.1:5349 \
  --tls-cert certificate.pem --tls-key private-key.pem
```

Provide your own PEM files and client-trusted certificate. The TLS listener
is additional to the UDP/TCP listener. This initial server does not renew
certificates or reload TLS files automatically.

## Check the installation

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn --version
./target/release/spry-turn --help
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
```

The socket suite starts its own loopback server instances, generated secret
and temporary TLS fixtures, then removes them. Build with `--features tls`
before using `--tls`. Browser and WASM validation commands are in
[contributing](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

If allocation succeeds but media does not arrive, check peer policy, UDP
relay reachability and credentials before changing client transports.
The [operations guide](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md) explains the current firewall and
relay-port limitations.

## Source: Client and host integration

Canonical source: [docs/integration.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md)

# Client and host integration

TURN is an optional transport choice in the calling application. The
application or independent operator selects the server and supplies a
short-lived credential pair. spry-turn supplies neither room admission
nor a hosted credential endpoint.

## Browser WebRTC

Use the browser's existing ICE implementation. This example takes a
credential pair already supplied by the selected operator:

```js
function relayConnection({ username, credential }) {
  return new RTCPeerConnection({
    iceServers: [{
      urls: [
        'turn:relay.example:3478?transport=udp',
        'turn:relay.example:3478?transport=tcp',
        'turns:relay.example:5349?transport=tcp',
      ],
      username,
      credential,
    }],
    iceTransportPolicy: 'relay',
  });
}
```

`relay.example` is a placeholder, not an included service. Only list
transports the operator has enabled and made reachable. `relay` forces
TURN for qualification; choose `all` if the application should also try
direct ICE paths. Media tracks, data channels, SDP exchange, consent,
end-to-end encryption and reconnect policy stay with the application.

The `transport=tcp` URLs describe client-to-server transport. The current
server still uses UDP allocations towards the peer. This is different
from TCP relay allocations under RFC 6062, which are not implemented.

The shared server secret must never be bundled into JavaScript, WASM, a
mobile app, a join URL or a browser storage entry. The WASM credential
helper is for trusted operator tools; it does not make exposing the secret
to clients safe.

## Native TURN clients

Existing native WebRTC clients can use the same ICE URLs, username and
password through their platform's ICE configuration. They do not need to
embed this library to use the server. Physical iOS, Android and no-Play
GrapheneOS acceptance against this implementation remain unverified.

## Embed the native Rust server

Rust applications can depend on the public Git repository.
Use a reviewed full commit SHA in place of `REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`:

```toml
[dependencies]
spry-turn = { git = "https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn.git", rev = "REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA" }
```

The following host starts a local server and advances its event loop:

```rust
use spry_turn::turn::{Config, Server};
use std::{io, time::Duration};

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let secret = std::env::var("SPRY_TURN_SECRET")
        .map_err(io::Error::other)?
        .into_bytes();
    let mut server = Server::bind(Config::local(secret))?;
    loop {
        server.poll_once(Duration::from_secs(1))?;
    }
}
```

The host owns scheduling, shutdown and credential storage. No worker
thread starts automatically. Drop the server to close its sockets. Use a
dedicated host thread if the surrounding application cannot block in
`poll_once`; Swift/Kotlin bindings are future work. Configuration fields
and feature combinations are listed in [the API reference](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md).

## Browser WASM packet codec

Build the module and glue using [the API commands](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md#wasm-build).
Serve these files through the embedding application's existing asset
pipeline; there is no project-operated CDN.

```js
import init, { PacketArena } from './spry_turn.js';

const wasm = await init();
const arena = new PacketArena(2048);
let bytes = new Uint8Array(wasm.memory.buffer, arena.ptr(), arena.capacity());
const payload = new TextEncoder().encode('hello');
bytes.set(payload, 4);
if (!arena.frame_channel(0x4000, payload.length)) {
  throw new Error('packet does not fit');
}
const length = payload.length + 4;
if (arena.channel_payload_len(length) !== payload.length) {
  throw new Error('invalid channel packet');
}
// Consume or send bytes.subarray(0, length) before reusing or freeing the arena.
// Recreate bytes after any WebAssembly memory growth.
arena.free();
```

Framing a packet does not create a TURN allocation or authorise channel
`0x4000`. A host adapter must implement session control and supply actual
I/O. Ordinary browser WASM cannot open the raw UDP/TCP sockets needed to
host a standard TURN server. The codec is useful for protocol adapters and
tests; it does not replace browser WebRTC.

## KithMoot, Archy and Sapflow

KithMoot may point its normal TURN client at an independently selected
instance. The optional [standalone pairing service](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/standalone.md) uses the
same access library as a host integration. Archipelago packages can consume
that library and supply their own signing-provider UI through `spry-service`.
Installation, exposure policy and mesh integration stay with the chosen host.
The publisher operates no default relay, directory or credential service.

Sapflow or another non-WebRTC application would need a TURN-aware transport
adapter. Standard TURN can carry arbitrary datagrams, but unmodified SRT
or RTMP clients do not become TURN clients by changing a destination URL.
No codecs, SRT, RTMP or HLS stack is included.

---

## Source: Standalone service and libraries

Canonical source: [docs/standalone.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/standalone.md)

# Standalone Spry and reusable libraries

Spry is a standalone ForgeSworn product. Its libraries and service are usable
without Archipelago. Other ForgeSworn products consume the same libraries;
Archipelago packages that product for its node owners.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `spry-turn` | Bounded packet forwarding, TURN authentication and protocol codecs; native library and standalone relay executable |
| `spry-access` | Owner-authorised pairing, scoped grants, short-lived credentials and private state; no network runtime |
| `spry-link` | Signed encrypted control messages, peer cards, packet frames and expiring scoped routes; no sockets or runtime |
| `spry-service` | Optional HTTP, Nostr and OS-ULA host adapters and standalone `spry-node` executable; supplied UI assets and explicit owner configuration |
| Archipelago package | Installation, node-supplied owner identities, host certificates, permissions and an optional dashboard signing provider |
| Calling application | Pairing consent, room membership, media keys, credential renewal and call controls |

The relay never imports the access service or Archipelago. The service uses
the access library and supervises the separate native relay executable.
Hosts can also embed the relay directly. Shared library configuration has no
hard-coded KithMoot origin allowlist; each host supplies its intended calling
application and any extra permitted origins. The standalone UI uses the
owner's existing NIP-07 signing extension. Archipelago can supply its own
signing-provider assets through the host adapter.

Build both standalone executables:

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --workspace --features tls
```

For the pairing service, supply `SPRY_PUBLIC_URL` (its HTTPS origin),
`SPRY_OWNER_KEYS` (comma-separated owner public keys), `SPRY_TURN_SECRET`
(at least 32 bytes) and `SPRY_RELAY_IP` (the relay's reachable IPv4 address).
Set `SPRY_STATE_FILE` to a private persistent file and, if needed,
`SPRY_KITHMOOT_URL` to the intended calling application's HTTPS URL.
`SPRY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` explicitly adds HTTPS origins for other clients.
`SPRY_ROOM_SEAL` (`auto`, the default, `required` or `off`; any other value
refuses startup) decides when a room grant admits only the signing keys its
paired app registered: once that app seals the grant, on every grant, or
never. It applies to both profiles; see the
[API reference](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md#room-grant-paths).
An operator who wants to serve anyone can turn on [public mode](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/public-mode.md)
in this standard profile; it is off by default and has no default relays.

`spry-node` listens on loopback HTTP port 3744 behind the operator's HTTPS
reverse proxy. That proxy must append or set `X-Forwarded-For`: requests
are rate-limited per caller before authentication, keyed on the right-most
entry (IPv6 grouped by /64), and without the header every caller shares the
proxy's one allowance. Authenticated requests also have a per-key limit, in
which owners and paired apps always keep a place. `spry-node` finds
`spry-turn` beside itself; `SPRY_RELAY_BINARY`
overrides that location. Standard TURN listeners and the bounded peer range
are described in the [operator guide](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md). Optional certificate
files for the relay reside under `/data/tls`; an external host adapter can
instead terminate TURN TLS. Setting `SPRY_TLS_GATE=true` advertises that
host's configured TLS transport and does not start or configure a TLS proxy.

No Archipelago daemon, node identity store, dashboard, container runtime or
FIPS installation is required for this standalone path. A reachable relay
and valid HTTPS still require operator configuration. The optional private-node profile below connects paired nodes over an existing
OS mesh route. It does not create that route or configure a router.

Networking integrations belong behind optional adapters. An Archipelago
adapter uses its existing mesh and host facilities; reusable improvements to
those facilities can be proposed upstream. Other hosts can supply a different
transport without importing Archipelago into Spry's forwarding or access
libraries.

Within Archipelago, the app manager owns package installation and lifecycle,
the existing identity/signing layer approves owner operations, the app gate
owns its HTTPS integration, and the networking layer owns mesh connectivity.
Those are the integration points for the relevant library or thin adapter.
Each library retains its own narrow purpose and independent build; installing
the package does not transfer those host responsibilities into Spry.

Git dependencies use a reviewed full commit SHA; see the
[access library](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/crates/spry-access/README.md) and
[native embedding guide](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md#embed-the-native-rust-server).
No new package registry publication is implied by these libraries.

## Private-node profile

For a Linux host with an existing IPv6 ULA route to the other nodes, set
`SPRY_PEER_INTERFACE` to that interface name, or set `SPRY_PEER_BIND` to its
explicit `[ULA]:3745` address. Keep `SPRY_RELAY_IP` as the concrete local IPv4
client listener, and set `SPRY_CLIENT_HOST` if clients use a different local
hostname. `SPRY_OWNER_URL` is the HTTPS owner UI origin. The host admits TCP
3745 on its private mesh interface; Spry requires no extra capabilities.

The service embeds the native forwarding library in this profile. Its
virtual relay addresses belong to 127.64.0.0/10, with UDP ports 49160–49191.
They are carried across authenticated peer links and must never be exposed
as arbitrary loopback proxies. Each node only accepts signed, unexpired peer
cards registered by one of its paired apps. Revoking that pairing withdraws
its routes. The core rejects host services, LAN addresses and arbitrary
Internet destinations in this profile.

Choose **Pair with KithMoot**. The owner signing provider supplies the person's
existing read/write Nostr relays; standalone hosts may explicitly configure
`SPRY_CONTROL_RELAYS` as a JSON array instead. Spry verifies connectivity before
issuing the pairing link and persists that selection for restarts. No extra
relay account, default directory or publisher-operated call server is added.
Control messages contain opaque access scopes and signed peer cards, without
room secrets or media keys. Media packets travel between nodes over their OS
route; Nostr carries control and the calling application's own signalling.

Only the explicitly paired node may return local client TURN addresses.
Foreign room adverts are verified offline and registered with that node;
clients must not contact foreign private endpoints or automatically open the
relays advertised by them. Everyone in a private-only call needs access to
their own paired node. A public TURN host remains an alternative for guests
without a reachable private node.

`SPRY_SOCKS_PROXY` optionally selects a SOCKS5 proxy for outbound control,
including remote DNS. A configured proxy has no direct-connect fallback.
`SPRY_CONTROL_CA_FILE` optionally adds a bounded PEM CA bundle to normal TLS
trust for explicitly selected control relays. Certificate and hostname
validation remain enabled. `SPRY_LOCAL_TEST=true` is for generated fixtures;
never enable it in a deployed node.

Run the independent packet test with `python3 tests/mesh.py --binary <Linux
mesh-node example> --output .local/mesh.json`. `tests/home-flow.mjs` additionally
drives actual standalone pairing screens and a built KithMoot PWA across
separate Linux containers, using generated audio/video and relay-only ICE.
Its receipt records the precise network and browser limits. Neither local
test substitutes for physical phones, the installed Archipelago bundle or
independent home broadband/NAT acceptance.

The [three-node browser receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/spry-private-nodes-browser-20261024.json)
records actual pairing, relay-only 1:1/group media, reload and fresh audio/video
progress after 330 seconds. The [packet receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/spry-private-nodes-packets-20261024.json)
separately records UDP/TCP forwarding and withdrawal on an isolated network
with no external connectivity. Both name their exact fixture limits.

The [creator-offline browser receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/spry-creator-offline-browser-20261024.json)
adds a fresh call after the room creator's browser closes and their actual
Spry container stops. Both remaining clients reload and start relay-only
audio/video, then continue receiving fresh media after 330 seconds. Run
`tests/home-flow.mjs` with `--kithmoot <checkout> --node-binary <Linux spry-node>
--output .local/creator-offline.json --nodes 3 --standing-seconds 330
--offline-creator true` to reproduce it. The generated signalling relay stays
available independently of the creator. This checks application behaviour
and credential renewal; the receipt retains the same browser/network limits.

A mesh whose routing needs an identity lookup can supply `SPRY_PEER_NAME`,
`SPRY_PEER_RESOLVER` (a loopback DNS socket) and `SPRY_PEER_ZONE`. The optional
adapter queries only that zone, binds the DNS response to its question and
transaction, and requires the returned AAAA address to equal the signed ULA.
It never substitutes an arbitrary DNS destination. Archipelago supplies the
seeded public mesh name and its existing FIPS resolver; Spry imports no mesh
SDK. The [FIPS/NAT packet receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/spry-fips-two-nats-20261024.json)
checks this adapter with two simulated home NATs, an isolated WAN and a
separate fixture mesh anchor. Spry containers retain no extra capabilities;
TUN and forwarding permissions belong to the fixture's host/network layer.

Reproduce that packet check with Docker and a Linux `mesh-node` example
matching the Docker engine's CPU architecture. Fetch the released FIPS
0.4.1 archive and verify it before extraction:

```sh
mkdir -p .local/fips-fixture
gh release download v0.4.1 --repo jmcorgan/fips \
  --pattern checksums-linux.txt --pattern fips-0.4.1-linux-aarch64.tar.gz \
  --dir .local/fips-fixture
(cd .local/fips-fixture && \
  grep '  fips-0.4.1-linux-aarch64.tar.gz$' checksums-linux.txt | sha256sum -c - && \
  tar -xzf fips-0.4.1-linux-aarch64.tar.gz --strip-components=1)
docker build -f tests/fixtures/fips/Dockerfile -t spry-fips-fixture:0.4.1 tests/fixtures/fips
cargo build --locked --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu \
  --example mesh-node -p spry-service
python3 tests/fips-mesh.py \
  --binary target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug/examples/mesh-node \
  --fips-dir .local/fips-fixture --output .local/fips-two-nats.json
```

On x86-64 Linux use the `linux-x86_64` archive and
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` Rust target instead. Cross-compiling requires a
Linux linker and sysroot (for example an installed `cargo-zigbuild`); on
macOS replace `cargo build` above with `cargo zigbuild`. Keep the existing
worktree's target directory. The fixture removes its containers, networks
and binary snapshot on exit. Remove downloaded binaries, archives and the
task-owned fixture image after retaining the required receipt privately.

## Source: Rust and WASM API

Canonical source: [docs/api.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md)

# Rust and WASM API reference

Version 0.3.0. Source is authoritative; there is no published crates.io,
docs.rs or npm package. Authorised users can generate local Rust API pages
with `cargo doc --locked --all-features --no-deps`.

## Cargo features

| Feature | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `runtime` | Native Mio sockets and OS randomness; by itself it does not enable TURN |
| `turn` | STUN/TURN wire codec, credential helpers and nonce logic |
| `direct-index` | Native runtime and TURN, with generation-tagged readiness slots |
| `connected-udp` | `direct-index` plus concrete-IPv4 connected-socket optimisation |
| `tls` | Native runtime, TURN and optional rustls TLS client listener |
| `wasm` | TURN helpers and wasm-bindgen; the exported arena is WASM-only |

Defaults are `runtime`, `turn` and `connected-udp`. Use
`--no-default-features --features runtime,turn` for the portable native
path, `--no-default-features --features turn --lib` for codec/auth only,
or `--no-default-features --features wasm --lib` for a WASM module. The
WASM build must exclude the native defaults.

## Native configuration

Source: [src/turn.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/turn.rs).

`Config::local(secret: Vec<u8>) -> Config` sets these defaults:

| Field | Default and purpose |
|---|---|
| `listen` | `127.0.0.1:3478`, shared UDP/TCP listening address |
| `relay_ip` | `127.0.0.1`, local bind address of UDP peer sockets |
| `relay_port_range` | `None` for OS ephemeral ports, or `Some((first, last))` for an inclusive nonzero UDP relay range with no fallback |
| `relay_port_mappings` | `None`; optional 1–1024 exact `RelayPortMapping` local/public UDP pairs, excluding range mode; see [mapped ports](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/mapped-ports.md) |
| `advertised_ip` | `None`; optional NAT-visible relay IP of the same address family |
| `realm` | `spry-turn`, long-term authentication realm |
| `secret` | Caller supplied, at least 32 bytes |
| `allow_loopback_peers` | `false`; explicit loopback testing |
| `max_allocations` | `1024`, total logical allocation limit |
| `max_per_user` | `8`, per-username allocation limit |
| `max_connections` | `256`, TCP/TLS connections |
| `bytes_per_second` | `67108864`, aggregate byte rate per allocation across both directions |
| `tls` | `None`; with `tls`, an optional address and `Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>` |

`Server::bind(config)` validates configuration and binds listeners. Realm
must contain 1–128 bytes, relay bind IP must be concrete and numeric limits
must be positive. A configured relay range requires `1 <= first <= last`;
port exhaustion produces TURN 508 without widening the range. The CLI additionally restricts loopback-peer opt-in to a
loopback-only listener; embedding hosts must enforce the same policy.

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `Server::bind(config: Config)` | `io::Result<Server>` |
| `server.local_addr()` | `io::Result<SocketAddr>` |
| `server.poll_once(timeout: Duration)` | `io::Result<()>`; processes readiness and expiry work |
| `server.stats()` | Copy of `limits::Stats` aggregate counters |
| `server.allocation_count()` | Current number of allocations |
| `turn::unix_time()` | Current epoch seconds |

The library starts no threads. A host must keep polling and drop `Server`
when it wants to close listeners and allocations. `Stats` contains
`forwarded_packets`, `forwarded_bytes` and `dropped_packets`; these are
process-local counters, not a remote monitoring or billing API.

## Wire and authentication helpers

Sources: [src/wire.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/wire.rs), [src/auth.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/auth.rs).

- `wire::Message::parse(&[u8]) -> Option<Message<'_>>`: borrowed STUN parser,
  with `method`, `class` and transaction ID; attributes remain borrowed.
- `message.attr(type)`, `number(type)` and `address(type)`: read attributes.
- `message.verify(key) -> bool`: verify message integrity.
- `wire::Builder::new(method, class, transaction)`: construct a STUN packet;
  `attr`, `number`, `address`, then `finish(key)` produce owned bytes.
- `wire::channel(&[u8]) -> Option<(u16, &[u8])>`: borrowed ChannelData parser.
- `wire::frame_len(&[u8]) -> Option<usize>`: obtain the declared stream frame
  length, including channel padding. Fewer than four bytes return `None`;
  an invalid leading type returns `Some(0)`. The caller must wait for that
  many bytes and validate the complete packet separately.
- `auth::credential(secret, username) -> String`: TURN REST password.
- `auth::key(username, realm, password) -> [u8; 16]`: long-term integrity key.
- `auth::expires(username) -> Option<u64>`: parse the expiry prefix.
- `auth::Nonces`: issue and validate time-, IP- and realm-bound nonces;
  `new()` uses OS randomness when `runtime` is enabled.

Parsing and integrity verification do not themselves grant a peer
permission, allocate a relay or enforce the application's membership.
For normal server use, let `Server` own the TURN state machine.

## Room-grant paths

Source: [crates/spry-access/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/crates/spry-access/src/lib.rs).

The `spry-node` service and `spry:` control channel pass these `POST`
bodies to `Authority::handle` after the usual signed-request check, body
limit and per-source and per-key rate limits. Every refusal is
`{"error":"<message>"}` with the status shown.

| Path | Signer | Body | Success |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/grants` | Paired app | `{"pairing","scope"}` | `{"v":1,"endpoint","token","expiresAt"}`; one grant per pairing and scope, renewed in place |
| `/v1/grants/remove` | Paired app | `{"pairing","grant"}` | `{"removed":true}`; drops the grant and its registered keys |
| `/v1/grants/devices` | The pairing that owns the grant | `{"v":1,"pairing","grant","add":[...],"remove":[...],"seal":true,"revision":N}` | `{"v":1,"sealed":bool,"enforced":bool,"devices":N}` |
| `/v1/grants/vouch` | A confirmed key on the grant | `{"v":1,"grant","add":[...]}` | `{"v":1,"added":N}` |
| `/v1/credentials` | Any key, or a registered key when enforced | `{"grant"}` | TURN `urls`, `username`, `credential`, `expiresAt` (at most 5 minutes) and `accessExpiresAt` |

`/v1/grants/devices` and `/v1/grants/vouch` refuse any field not shown and
any `v` other than 1 (400 "Invalid request."). Keys are distinct lowercase
64-hex x-only public keys that are valid curve points.

- `/v1/grants/devices`: at most 32 keys in each of `add` and `remove`, no key
  in both; `seal` optional; `revision` an integer up to 2^53 - 1 that must
  exceed the last one accepted for the grant in the past 90 seconds (else
  409 "Out of date. Try again."). A signer that does not hold the named
  pairing, or a grant of another pairing, gets 403 "Approval required.";
  an unknown or expired grant gets 403 "Call access has expired.". An added
  key becomes a confirmed entry with a 30-day lease, replacing a vouched
  entry for it. A removed key loses its entry and its device slot at once.
  `seal: true` seals the grant for good; `false` never unseals. Changes apply
  all or nothing: a request refused for capacity also drops its removals
  and its seal. Clients should therefore send removals, and a seal, in a
  request of their own rather than with adds.
- `/v1/grants/vouch`: one to four keys. The signer must hold a confirmed,
  unexpired entry, else 403 "Call access has expired.". A key already listed
  is left as it is; any other gains a vouched entry that lapses 24 hours
  later, is never renewed by use and cannot vouch. Every named key counts
  against the caps, listed or not, and `added` is the number of keys named,
  so the answer does not reveal which keys were listed. At most 8 vouched
  entries per grant at once, 8 vouches per signer per grant per 24 hours
  and 64 signers tracked per grant; these and the grant, pairing and node
  limits below all refuse with 429 "Spry is busy. Try again shortly.". A
  vouch never evicts.
- `/v1/credentials`: an enforced grant refuses a key without an unexpired
  entry with 403 "Call access has expired.", the same refusal as an expired
  grant, before counting it against the 32 concurrent device slots. A
  confirmed entry's lease renews to 30 days on use once fewer than 29 days
  remain.

A grant is enforced when `Config::seal` is `Required`, or when it is `Auto`
(the default) and the grant is sealed. `Off` stores registrations and
vouches but never enforces them. `spry-node` reads this from
`SPRY_ROOM_SEAL` (`auto`, `required` or `off`) once at startup.

A grant holds at most 64 registered keys, the grants of one pairing at most
512 together (half the node) and the node at most 1024. Adding to a full
grant evicts the confirmed entry with no live device slot that was used
least recently since start; with none to evict it refuses with 429 "This
call has reached its device limit.". Over the pairing's share or the node
limit it refuses with 429 "Spry is already helping too many calls.". Registered keys persist
in the state file as `"sealed":true` and `"members":[["<key>",<lease end>,
<vouched>]]` on each grant; the file stays version 1 and within its 131072
byte limit, and an older binary loads it with every grant unsealed.

## WASM build

```sh
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo build --locked --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  --no-default-features --features wasm --lib
wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir .local/wasm --out-name spry_turn \
  target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/spry_turn.wasm
node tests/wasm.mjs
```

Use wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129 to match the pinned crate. Install that
specific CLI version if needed; the server does not depend on the CLI at
runtime. The generated package contains `.wasm`, JavaScript and TypeScript
declarations. See [integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md#browser-wasm-packet-codec).

Source: [src/wasm.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/wasm.rs).

| JavaScript API | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `new PacketArena(capacity)` | Allocate 20–65,536 bytes once |
| `arena.ptr()` / `arena.capacity()` | Location and length for a borrowed `Uint8Array` |
| `arena.valid_stun(len)` | Validate a STUN packet in the arena |
| `arena.stun_method(len)` / `stun_class(len)` | Parsed value, or `-1` |
| `arena.verify_integrity(len, key)` | Verify an in-arena STUN packet |
| `arena.frame_channel(number, payloadLen)` | Write a ChannelData header; payload starts at offset 4 |
| `arena.channel_number(len)` / `channel_payload_len(len)` | Parsed value, or `-1` |
| `arena.free()` | Release the arena; invalidate all borrowed views |
| `rest_credential(secret, username)` | Trusted operator credential helper |

Channel numbers accepted by this initial codec are `0x4000`–`0x4fff`.
The caller owns networking, channel allocation and session authorisation.
Do not retain views across WASM memory growth or past `arena.free()`.
Credential helpers are not for placing a server secret into a public client.

---

## Source: Coturn compatibility

Canonical source: [docs/coturn-compatibility.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/coturn-compatibility.md)

# Coturn compatibility and migration

spry-turn implements a focused subset of STUN/TURN. It has no coturn
configuration-file parser and is not a universal drop-in replacement.
The goal is a small forwarding core with measured resource costs.

## Feature map

| Coturn deployment need | spry-turn 0.2.0 |
|---|---|
| STUN Binding | Implemented |
| TURN UDP relay allocations | Implemented |
| UDP clients | Implemented and socket/browser tested |
| TCP clients | Implemented and socket/browser tested |
| TLS clients | Optional `tls` feature; socket/browser tested with generated certificates |
| Expiring shared-secret TURN REST credentials | Implemented; operator-run credential command |
| Allocate, Refresh and explicit deallocation | Implemented |
| IP permissions, ChannelBind and ChannelData | Implemented |
| Send and Data indications | Implemented |
| IPv4 or IPv6 relay sockets | One configured family per instance; IPv6 field acceptance remains open |
| Allocation, per-user, connection and bandwidth limits | Implemented; names and semantics differ from coturn |
| NAT-advertised relay IP | `--public-ip`; actual NAT mapping is operator responsibility |
| Static long-term username/password database | Not implemented |
| Fixed UDP relay-port range | `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`; exhaustion fails with 508, no ephemeral fallback |
| Dual allocations, EVEN-PORT and reservation tokens | Not implemented |
| RFC 8489 SHA-256 authentication | Not implemented |
| TCP relay allocations (RFC 6062) | Not implemented |
| DTLS client transport | Not implemented |
| OAuth, database backends, clustering, HTTP/telnet administration | Not implemented |
| Certificate renewal or reload | Not implemented |

Unknown comprehension-required attributes receive a 420 response. See
[GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md) for qualification and remaining extensions.

## Configuration concepts

These are conceptual mappings, not a compatible configuration syntax:

| Coturn concept | spry-turn equivalent |
|---|---|
| `listening-ip` and `listening-port` | `--listen IP:PORT` |
| `relay-ip` | `--relay-ip IP` |
| `min-port` / `max-port` | Inclusive `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`; no coturn configuration-file parsing |
| `external-ip` | `--public-ip IP`; no automatic mapping discovery |
| `realm` | `--realm NAME` |
| `use-auth-secret` / `static-auth-secret` | Required `SPRY_TURN_SECRET` environment variable |
| `total-quota` | `--max-allocations COUNT` |
| `user-quota` | `--max-per-user COUNT` |
| `max-bps` | `--bytes-per-second COUNT`; assess aggregate accounting and burst behaviour separately |
| TLS listener/certificate/key | `--tls-listen`, `--tls-cert`, `--tls-key` with a TLS-enabled build |

For shared-secret clients, retain the expiry-prefixed username format and
HMAC-generated password. Do not reuse application identity or room IDs as
transport labels. The realm and nonce are server-owned authentication
inputs; coturn's live sessions and nonces are not transferred.

## Assess a deployment before switching

1. List the exact transports, authentication mode, relay address family,
   firewall port range and extensions your current clients require.
2. Compare that list with the feature map. A deployment needing a missing
   feature should continue using its current server.
3. Run an independent instance and configure an explicit test client with
   separate credentials. Do not redirect active calls during evaluation.
4. Test both endpoints, forced relay, actual decoded media/data, credential
   renewal, UDP blocking, long calls, reconnects and trusted TLS certificates.
5. Size file descriptors for the additional connected-UDP socket and test
   exhaustion and peer restrictions on the intended host/network.
6. Retain the existing ICE configuration as a rollback path. Switching a
   server address does not transfer existing allocations or guarantee ICE
   restart behaviour in an application.

## Measured performance

The native ARM64 M4 Max UDP loopback matrix recorded 17–22% higher packet
throughput than the tested coturn 4.18.0 configuration. CPU and process RSS
were lower; the optimisation also used more UDP sockets. These results
apply to the recorded workload and configuration, not all coturn uses.
See [benchmarks](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md) for latency, methodology, architecture
checks, descriptor counts, raw evidence and explicitly superseded runs.

---

## Source: Public mode

Canonical source: [docs/public-mode.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/public-mode.md)

# Public mode

Draft profile, version 1. Not a ratified NIP. Kind 31478 is a draft
allocation chosen for this profile and may change before any NIP proposal.

Public mode lets an independent operator open their own Spry relay to
anyone, and lets clients find it over Nostr. It is off unless the operator
turns it on. The software publisher runs no relay, credential service,
directory, index or default Nostr relay for it, and does not approve, rank
or list operators.

An operator who turns public mode on runs their own public service and is
responsible for it under the law where they and their users are. Spry does
not decide that for them. For the GB position see jurisdiction-kit's
[online-services note](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/law/gb/online-services.md),
sections 2.11 (transport) and 2.13 (discovery).

## What changes when it is on

| | Off (default) | On |
|---|---|---|
| Who can get TURN credentials | Paired apps with a room grant | Also anyone, through the public endpoint |
| Advert on Nostr | None | Only if the operator names relays to publish to |
| Pairing, grants, private-node routes | Unchanged | Unchanged |

Public credentials grant TURN relaying only. They give no pairing, grant,
room, peer route or owner authority, and they are not linked to any of
those.

## Operator configuration

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SPRY_PUBLIC=true` | Turn public mode on. Any other value, or unset, leaves it off |
| `SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS` | JSON array of `wss://` relays to publish the advert to. Unset: public but unlisted (no advert) |
| `SPRY_PUBLIC_REGION` | Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code the operator chooses to state, such as `GB` |
| `SPRY_PUBLIC_NOTE` | Optional operator text, at most 140 bytes, shown to people choosing a relay |
| `SPRY_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL` | Optional link to the operator's own privacy notice, published on open adverts as `["privacy", url]` |

There is no default relay list, region, note or privacy link. Spry never
fills these in, and never fetches the privacy link.

`SPRY_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL` must be an `https://` address on a DNS name of two
or more lowercase labels, with a path, at most 256 bytes: for example
`https://operator.example/privacy`, or `https://operator.example/` for the
site's front page (the trailing `/` is required). It may not carry userinfo,
a port, a query, a fragment, a percent-escape, an uppercase or `xn--` label,
an IP address, a reserved suffix such as `.local`, or an empty, `.` or `..`
path segment. Spry refuses to start, naming the setting, when it is invalid.
It is published only on open adverts, so only when `SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS` is
set. Its host need not be the relay's.

If you have no relays of your own in mind, these widely read public relays
accepted connections on 25 October 2026. They are run by other people, are
not checked or endorsed by the Spry project, and are only an example to
choose from; Spry does not use them unless you set them:

```sh
SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS='["wss://relay.damus.io","wss://relay.primal.net","wss://nostr-pub.wellorder.net","wss://relay.nostr.info"]'
```

Relays that charge for writing, such as `wss://nostr.wine`, will not take
the advert unless you are a member.

`SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS` follows the same rules as `SPRY_CONTROL_RELAYS`: one to
four distinct `wss://` URLs on DNS hostnames. Spry refuses to start, naming
the setting, when a value is invalid. To publish an advert, `SPRY_PUBLIC_URL`
must be an `https://` DNS hostname with no port, because clients refuse
anything else (client rule 4).

Public mode is v1 for the standard profile, where the relay allocates
ordinary addresses on the operator's public IP. The private-node profile
keeps its relay addresses on loopback behind peer links (127.64.0.0/10), so
v1 refuses to start with `SPRY_PUBLIC=true` in that profile, with a clear
error, rather than half-working. The other `SPRY_PUBLIC_*` settings are
ignored in that profile.

### Separate standard profiles on one host

The standard profile resolves these transport settings once at startup,
whether public mode is on or off:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SPRY_HTTP_PORT` | `3744` | Loopback HTTP API port behind the operator's HTTPS proxy |
| `SPRY_TURN_PORT` | `3478` | UDP and TCP TURN listener port |
| `SPRY_TLS_PORT` | `5349` | Direct TLS listener and advertised TLS port |
| `SPRY_RELAY_PORTS` | `49160:49191` | Inclusive UDP allocation port range |
| `SPRY_BYTES_PER_SECOND` | `1000000` | Per-allocation aggregate payload budget, in bytes per second, across both directions |

TURN and TLS ports must be decimal integers from 1 to 65535, must differ,
and must lie outside the ordered, non-zero relay range. The bandwidth must
be a decimal integer from 1 to 67108864; zero, overflow, signs and spaces
are refused with the setting's name. The private-node profile keeps its
existing settings and limits; it does not read the new standard-only
`SPRY_TLS_PORT`, `SPRY_RELAY_PORTS` or `SPRY_BYTES_PER_SECOND` settings.

For example, an operator can keep an existing paired instance and give a
separate public, unlisted standard instance its own ports and state:

```sh
SPRY_PUBLIC=true
SPRY_PUBLIC_URL=https://relay.example:3746
SPRY_HTTP_PORT=3746
SPRY_TURN_PORT=3479
SPRY_TLS_PORT=5350
SPRY_RELAY_PORTS=49200:49231
SPRY_BYTES_PER_SECOND=8388608
SPRY_TLS_GATE=true
```

These settings complement the required owner keys, fresh TURN secret,
reachable relay address and separate persistent state file described in
[standalone setup](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/standalone.md). Do not set a private peer bind or
interface on the public instance. Keep all API, listener and allocation
ports distinct from the other service, including its private peer port.
The two instances must have separate secrets and state files.

`SPRY_TLS_GATE=true` advertises TLS; the operator must provide a trusted
TLS gate at the selected TLS port forwarding to this instance's TCP TURN
port. With both existing `/data/tls/fullchain.pem` and
`/data/tls/privkey.pem` present, Spry instead starts its own TLS listener
on the selected TLS port. Configure the host's proxy, certificates,
firewall and any catalogue port mapping separately; setting an environment
variable does not open or route a host port.

The child relay's arguments, issued TURN URLs and UDP Binding readiness
probe use the same settings. An unavailable configured TURN port keeps
this instance unready; another instance listening elsewhere cannot make
it ready. Readiness checks the live child and a valid Binding response,
not the external TLS gate or public network route.

The rate is per allocation, with one second of burst capacity, rather than
a global server cap. The existing bounds remain 32 allocations, 8 per
username and 32 client connections; size host resources separately. An
8 MiB/s aggregate allocation budget can carry two directions sharing that
budget, but it is not a measured throughput promise.

Custom ports are for explicitly configured clients. They do not broaden
the signed advert rules: discovery still requires an HTTPS endpoint with
no port, and TURN ports from the existing allowlist in client rule 4.
Keep `SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS` unset for the custom-port example above.

## Public credential endpoint

`POST /v1/public/credentials`, body exactly `{"v":1}` (at most 256 bytes),
`Content-Type: application/json`. No `Authorization` header. Any `Origin` is
accepted for this path only; the response, including a refusal and the
`OPTIONS` preflight, carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and no
credentials mode. Every other path keeps its existing origin rules. With
public mode off the path does not exist: every method gets 404.

Response 200:

```json
{"urls":["turn:relay.example:3478?transport=udp","turn:relay.example:3478?transport=tcp","turns:relay.example:5349?transport=tcp"],
 "username":"1793000000:pub-0123456789abcdef01234567",
 "credential":"<base64 HMAC-SHA1>",
 "expiresAt":1793000000}
```

- Lifetime 3600 seconds. The relay ends an allocation when its login
  expires and refuses to refresh it after that, so a login bounds how long
  a call can use it. A client whose call may outlast the login fetches a
  fresh one before `expiresAt` and restarts ICE with it; a call that ends
  sooner needs nothing more.
- The username label is fresh random bytes for each issue. It is not derived
  from the caller's address, origin, any key or any earlier issue, so two
  credentials cannot be linked by their usernames.
- Limits, all in memory and swept: at most 32 issues per minute in total,
  6 per source address per minute, 256 tracked source addresses. Over a
  limit: 429 with a generic message. These limits are separate from the
  ones that protect pairing and paired apps.
- The service listens only on loopback behind the operator's HTTPS reverse
  proxy, so the source address is the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry,
  the one that proxy appended; without one, the connecting address. IPv6
  sources are grouped by /64. Configure the proxy to append or set that
  header; a proxy that passes a caller's own header through lets callers
  evade the per-source limit, though not the total.
- Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Nothing about the request, the caller or the issued username is logged or
  persisted. Startup and error diagnostics only.
- When the relay is not ready, 503 with the existing readiness message.

The relay's existing allocation, per-user, bandwidth and capacity limits
apply to public users as to anyone else.

## Advert

A Nostr addressable event signed by the node's transport identity (the
`spry-link` identity, separate from the owner's signing key):

```json
{"kind":31478,
 "tags":[["d","spry-turn"],["v","1"],["status","open"],["auth","public"],
         ["expiration","1793007200"],["g","GB"],
         ["privacy","https://operator.example/privacy"]],
 "content":"{\"credentials\":\"https://relay.example/v1/public/credentials\",\"urls\":[\"turn:relay.example:3478?transport=udp\",\"turn:relay.example:3478?transport=tcp\",\"turns:relay.example:5349?transport=tcp\"],\"note\":\"Optional operator text\"}"}
```

- `d` is always `spry-turn`: one advert per transport identity.
- `status` is `open` or `withdrawn`. `auth` is `public` in v1.
- `expiration` (NIP-40) is at most two hours after `created_at`. Spry sets
  it to exactly two hours.
- `g` appears only on an open advert, and only if the operator set
  `SPRY_PUBLIC_REGION`.
- `privacy` appears only on an open advert, and only if the operator set
  `SPRY_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL`. Like `g`, a reader refuses the whole advert if
  the tag is repeated, has other than two items or holds a link outside the
  rules above, wherever it appears. Readers that predate it ignore it, so
  the advert stays version 1.
- `content` holds the credential endpoint, the TURN URLs and the optional
  note. A withdrawn advert has `content` `{}`.
- It never contains credentials, the TURN secret, owner keys, pairings,
  rooms, participants, usage counts or call records.

Lifecycle:

- Publish when the relay first reports ready, then every 30 minutes, each
  time with a fresh `created_at` and `expiration`.
- If the relay stops being ready while the service runs, for example
  because its process died, publish a newer `withdrawn` advert within a few
  seconds, waiting at most 5 seconds for relays. When it is ready again,
  publish a fresh `open` advert and resume the 30-minute cycle.
- On graceful shutdown, publish a newer `withdrawn` advert before stopping,
  waiting at most 5 seconds. Every advert's `created_at` is later than the
  one before, even within the same second.
- When public mode is turned off, the next start publishes a `withdrawn`
  advert if `SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS` is still set. Spry keeps no record of
  earlier adverts, so with the relays also removed, or if the whole service
  stops abruptly, the last advert expires within two hours.
- Withdrawals are best effort: a relay that misses one keeps the last open
  advert until it expires, while the endpoint answers 503.
- Publish only to `SPRY_PUBLIC_RELAYS`, using the existing control-relay
  connection rules (TLS validation, SOCKS option, public-address checks). A
  relay that refuses or fails is retried on the next cycle; failures are not
  reported anywhere.

## Client rules

These bind any client that reads the adverts, including KithMoot. KithMoot's
own change gate applies before it builds this.

1. Read kind 31478 only from relays the user already uses or has chosen.
   No publisher default discovery relay, directory or index.
2. Verify the event id and signature, kind, `d`, `v` = `1` and `auth`.
   Refuse events over 4 KiB, `created_at` more than 10 minutes in the
   future, a missing `expiration`, an `expiration` that is not 1 to 16
   ASCII digits (no sign, space or other character), or an `expiration` in
   the past or more than two hours after `created_at`.
3. Keep, per transport key, the newest `created_at` seen (a replay
   watermark). Ignore anything not newer, including a repeat of the same
   event. A newer `withdrawn` advert removes the relay; an older `open` one
   cannot restore it. A watermark may be forgotten two hours after its
   `created_at`, since anything older has expired by then.
   A client that keeps watermarks across restarts may store, with each,
   the id of the event that set it, and after restoring accept that one
   identical event once without moving the watermark, so a chosen relay
   works before the operator next republishes. Anything older, and any
   other event with the same `created_at`, is still refused.
4. The credential endpoint must be exactly
   `https://<DNS hostname>/v1/public/credentials` in canonical form: no
   userinfo, port (not even `:443`), query, fragment or other path, and no
   `xn--` label. Refuse IP literals and names that resolve to private, loopback, link-local or
   reserved addresses. Every TURN URL (`turn:` over UDP or TCP, `turns:`
   over TCP, at most four) must use the same hostname, and a port of
   exactly `3478`, `5349` or `443`, or none for the scheme's default. Do
   not follow redirects.
5. Consider at most 64 adverts and contact at most 3 credential endpoints
   for one call. Never probe every advertised endpoint.
6. Choose and rank locally. Send no choice, latency, failure or usage report
   to the publisher or anyone else.
7. A signature shows which key made the statement. It does not show the
   operator's identity, honesty, uptime, logging or jurisdiction; `g` and
   `privacy` are the operator's own claims. Show them as such.
8. A privacy link is the operator's own; never fetch it without the person
   tapping it, and send no referrer. Show its hostname, label it as the
   operator's, and do not prefetch, preconnect, preview or persist it.
9. Reading an advert grants nothing. Credentials come only from the chosen
   operator's endpoint, and room admission stays with the calling app.

`spry_link::advert` implements rules 2 to 4, the privacy-link grammar
(`privacy_valid`) and the watermark (`verify` and the bounded `AdvertBook`),
so clients and fixtures share one implementation. It opens no sockets, so the resolution part of rule 4
remains the client's job when it connects.

## Fixtures

The standalone service tests start the real relay executable from this
source tree. Build it before running workspace tests:

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --features tls --bin spry-turn
SPRY_TEST_RELAY_BINARY=target/release/spry-turn cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features
```

`SPRY_TEST_RELAY_BINARY` is relative to the workspace root unless absolute;
without it, tests use `target/release/spry-turn` (with the platform's
executable suffix). A missing binary fails with the build command. The
tests use generated ports and synthetic secrets, exercise two distinct
profiles and their own readiness, and verify issued credentials against
real authenticated allocations. They do not qualify a public deployment
or an operator's TLS gate. CI builds the same source's TLS relay before
these tests and reuses that build for interop.

`crates/spry-link/examples/public-advert.rs` writes signed fixtures from a
fixed test key to `docs/fixtures/public-advert-v1.json`: a valid open advert,
a valid withdrawal, and invalid cases (bad signature, missing expiration,
expiration too far ahead, future `created_at`, an `expiration` with a sign,
IP-literal endpoint, mismatched TURN host, a TURN port outside the allowed
three, older open after newer withdrawn, the same advert twice, an `xn--`
credential host), a valid open advert with a privacy link, a withdrawal
carrying a valid privacy tag (`withdrawn`, link exposed), and privacy links
that are refused (over `http:`, with userinfo, a port, query, fragment,
percent-escape, backslash, uppercase host, trailing dot, IPv4 or IPv6
literal, `xn--` label, reserved or numeric last label, `?` or `#` before the
path, no path or a dot segment, a repeated or one-item `privacy` tag, or an
invalid tag on a withdrawal, each `Destination`; over 256 bytes, `Size`). Each case lists
events to give, in order, to a fresh watermark at the file's `now`, with the
expected verdict for each: `open`, `withdrawn` or the refusal's name, and in
`privacy` the link a verifier must expose for each, or null. Readers that
predate `privacy` accept the privacy-link cases' events as open adverts;
that is harmless, since they never show the link. Signing uses fixed auxiliary bytes, so regenerating
gives the same file. Clients test against that file.
